Document Title: Seismic Dip Estimation With a Domain Knowledge Constrained Transfer Learning Approach
Authors: Y. Ao; W. Lu; P. Xu; B. Jiang
Author Affiliations: Institute for Artificial Intelligence (THUAI), State Key Laboratory of Intelligent Technology and Systems, Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology (BNRIST), Tsinghua University, Beijing, China; Institute for Artificial Intelligence (THUAI), State Key Laboratory of Intelligent Technology and Systems, Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology (BNRIST), Tsinghua University, Beijing, China; Institute for Artificial Intelligence (THUAI), State Key Laboratory of Intelligent Technology and Systems, Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology (BNRIST), Tsinghua University, Beijing, China; Institute for Artificial Intelligence (THUAI), State Key Laboratory of Intelligent Technology and Systems, Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology (BNRIST), Tsinghua University, Beijing, China
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
Abstract: Accurate estimation of volumetric seismic dip is of great significance for subsequent seismic processing and interpretation works. Recently, with the development of deep learning techniques, convolutional networks are also applied for seismic dip estimation. Compared with traditional approaches, estimating dips with convolutional networks is not only more efficient but also shows great promise in accuracy and robustness. However, if we take dips estimated by traditional approaches as labels and train networks on the field seismic data directly, the accuracy and robustness of learned networks are influenced due to the error in dip labels. An alternative solution is synthesizing realistic seismic samples with accurate dip labels. However, we find that due to the differences in seismic responses and structural patterns between the synthetic and field seismic data, networks directly learned from synthetic samples cannot guarantee their generalization on the field seismic data. To overcome these drawbacks, we develop a transfer learning approach for improvement. The proposed approach pretrains the dip estimation network on synthetic seismic samples at first and then transfers it to the targeted field seismic data with a domain knowledge-inspired fine-tuning process. Moreover, the proposed approach also highlights the combination of deep learning techniques and domain knowledge in seismic processing—several subtle realizations, such as knowledge-driven sample augmentation, knowledge constrained loss function, and knowledge motivated transfer learning strategy, are introduced, which greatly enhance the learning of the seismic dip estimation network. The advantages of the proposed approach in accuracy, robustness, and resolution are validated by applying the estimated dips for structural filtering and curvature extraction on the Netherlands F3 and Kerry3D seismic data, which further confirms its practicality in the real-world application. We believe that the proposed approach has provided an effective improved way for further seismic dip estimation practices, and the present domain knowledge constrained deep learning case will also inspire researchers in the same discipline.

Document Title: Self-Supervised Few-Shot Modulation Recognition With Adversarial Representation Learning and Mixture of Experts
Authors: Y. Cai; S. Wu; Y. Lei; M. Shao; D. Li; S. Hong; J. Qi; H. Sun
Author Affiliations: School of Electronic Science and Engineering and the School of Informatics, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China; School of Informatics, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China; School of Informatics, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China; School of Electronic Science and Engineering, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China; School of Informatics, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China; School of Informatics, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China; School of Electronic Science and Engineering, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China; School of Informatics, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Fujian, China
Publication Title: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive Communications and Networking
Abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized automatic modulation classification (AMC), yet its reliance on large-scale, closed-set datasets remains a critical bottleneck, as these models generally perform poorly when training data is scarce or when faced with open-set scenarios. Few-shot learning (FSL) offers a promising solution by enabling models to grasp the concepts of new classes using only a limited number of labeled samples. In this paper, we propose a self-supervised FSL framework with gradient-adversarial data augmentation (GADA), tailored for modulation classification tasks. Our framework integrates a Transformer-LSTM hybrid encoder pre-trained through self-supervised learning on unlabeled base classes to capture universal temporal dependencies, combined with knowledge distillation and adversarial augmentation that generates gradient-guided perturbed samples to enhance feature robustness. Furthermore, we introduce two complementary ensemble strategies to enhance predictive performance under few-shot conditions. First, we propose a Mixture of Experts module augmented with shared experts (SMoE) to capture common knowledge, coupled with an auxiliary Exclusive Expert Entropy Loss ( $E^{3}$  Loss) that encourages task-specific experts to learn diverse and specialized representations. Second, we design a soft-voting ensemble that aggregates predictions from multiple independently fine-tuned classifiers, leading to more robust final decisions. Experimental validation on the RML2018.10a and RML2016.10a datasets demonstrates state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, achieving 96.07% accuracy and 94.01% in standard FSL scenarios. Notably, our approach consistently outperforms conventional FSL baselines across various signal conditions, demonstrating a significant advantage. These results validate our framework’s ability to simultaneously address two critical challenges: reducing dependence on labeled data while maintaining robust discriminative power across diverse signal environments.

Document Title: What Are Effective Labels for Augmented Data? Improving Calibration and Robustness with AutoLabel
Authors: Y. Qin; X. Wang; B. Lakshminarayanan; E. H. Chi; A. Beutel
Author Affiliations: Google Research; Google Research; Google Research; Google Research; Google Research
Publication Title: 2023 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)
Abstract: A wide breadth of research has devised data augmentation approaches that can improve both accuracy and generalization performance for neural networks. However, augmented data can end up being far from the clean training data and what is the appropriate label is less clear. Despite this, most existing work simply uses one-hot labels for augmented data. In this paper, we show re-using one-hot labels for highly distorted data might run the risk of adding noise and degrading accuracy and calibration. To mitigate this, we propose a generic method AutoLabel to automatically learn the confidence in the labels for augmented data, based on the transformation distance between the clean distribution and augmented distribution. AutoLabel is built on label smoothing and is guided by the calibration-performance over a hold-out validation set. We successfully apply AutoLabel to three different data augmentation techniques: the state-of-the-art RandAug, AugMix, and adversarial training. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet show that AutoLabel significantly improves existing data augmentation techniques over models' calibration and accuracy, especially under distributional shift. Additionally, AutoLabel improves adversarial training by bridging the gap between clean accuracy and adversarial robustness.

Document Title: Mobile-AMT: Real-Time Polyphonic Piano Transcription for In-the-Wild Recordings
Author Affiliations: Music Informatics Group, R&D Division, Yamaha Corporation, Shizuoka, Japan; Music Informatics Group, R&D Division, Yamaha Corporation, Shizuoka, Japan
Abstract: This paper introduces a polyphonic piano transcription framework that can robustly transcribe piano notes from real-world audio recordings in real time. State-of-the-art (SoTA) automatic music transcription (AMT) methods lack real-time processing capabilities and generalization to unseen recording conditions, making them difficult to deploy in a real-world scenario. To address these challenges, we propose mobile-AMT, a new AMT framework that consists of 1) an online and lightweight network architecture with efficient recurrent and convolutional layers, and 2) a data augmentation scheme to enhance robustness against out-of-domain recordings. The mobile-AMT model reduces the computational cost by 82.9% while retaining comparable accuracy to the recent SoTA method, allowing real-time AMT on mobile devices. The proposed augmentation improves the note F1-score by 14.3 points when evaluated on realistic audio with various recording conditions.

Document Title: ShadowGPT: Linguistic Fingerprinting for Robust Detection of AI-Generated Phishing Emails
Publication Title: 2025 IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference (URTC)
Abstract: This paper presents ShadowGPT, a novel machine learning system for detecting ChatGPT-generated phishing emails through linguistic fingerprinting. As ChatGPT-3.5 become increasingly accessible, malicious actors exploit them to create sophisticated phishing campaigns that evade traditional detection methods. Our approach extracts 4 4 distinctive linguistic features encompassing stylometric patterns, readability metrics, vocabulary diversity, syntactic structures, and semantic indicators. We developed a robust gradient boosting classifier trained on 6,749 emails comprising 831 ChatGPT-generated phishing samples, 1,660 human-written phishing emails, and 4,258 legitimate communications. The training process incorporated noise augmentation to ensure real-world resilience. ShadowGPT achieves 99.6% accuracy with a 95% confidence interval of 99.2% to 99.8% in binary classification while maintaining an exceptionally low 0.14% false positive rate. The system demonstrates remarkable robustness, maintaining 99% accuracy under 20% feature perturbation. Our analysis reveals that ChatGPT-generated phishing exhibits consistent patterns including moderate urgency scores (0.98 ± 0.73), elevated trust language (0.70 ± 0.81), complex readability (Flesch: 23.9 ± 26.1), and low vocabulary diversity (0.684). These findings demonstrate that ChatGPT-3.5-generated phishing possesses detectable linguistic fingerprints, enabling effective defense against this emerging threat.

Document Title: A Design of a Histopathology Image Augmentation Pipeline for Colon Cancer Image Processing
Authors: J. Li; W. Goh; N. Jhanjhi
Author Affiliations: Digital Health and Medical Advancement Impact Lab, School of Computer Science, Taylor's University, Subang Jaya, Malaysia; Digital Health and Medical Advancement Impact Lab, School of Computer Science, Taylor's University, Subang Jaya, Malaysia; Digital Health and Medical Advancement Impact Lab, School of Computer Science, Taylor's University, Subang Jaya, Malaysia
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Networks and Computer Communications (ETNCC)
Abstract: Robust data augmentation is essential for training histopathology classifiers that generalize across scanners, centers and staining protocols. We evaluated three augmentation pipelines on 204 colon-tissue tiles from the LC25000 collection, benchmarking realism with Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and colour fidelity with mean lightness drift ($\Delta L^{*}$). A stain-only strategy, Macenko normalization plus direct stain transfer, produced the poorest match to the original distribution (FID $\approx 37.4$, $\left.\Delta L^{*} \approx 5.10\right)$, indicating that color manipulations alone can severely distort global image statistics. Adding purely geometric and mild morphological transforms (flips, small rotations, elastic shifts) sharply reduced both metrics (FID $\approx 13.8, \Delta L^{*} \approx 1.27$) while preserving diagnostic appearance. Building on this baseline with an AugMix-light branch yielded only a modest rise in FID $(\approx 16.4)$ and $\Delta L^{*}(\approx 1.45)$ yet injected richer local contrast and color variation-attributes that improve robustness to scanner and slide-ageing artifacts. Qualitative inspection confirmed that nuclei, gland borders and stromal textures remained intact across all augmented sets. These findings advocate a tiered augmentation curriculum: prioritize shape-preserving operations to anchor photometric realism, then layer in blended low-severity transforms for diversity, while monitoring both distributional and color metrics to avoid overshooting. The proposed recipe balances realism with variability, offering a practical path toward more generalizable and trustworthy computational pathology models.

Document Title: A Two-Phase Data Augmentation Strategy with Mixup and AugMix
Author Affiliations: Faculty of Engineering, The University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia
Publication Title: 2025 International Conference on Computers, Information Processing and Advanced Education (CIPAE)
Abstract: Deep neural networks have driven considerable progress in image classification, improving predictive accuracy across a wide range of benchmarks. However, distribution shifts caused by noise, blur, or contrast variations can substantially reduce model accuracy, making robustness to such corruptions a critical objective. To this end, this paper proposes a two-phase data augmentation strategy termed Mixup-AugMix. The early training phase applies Mixup to smooth decision boundaries. The later training phase retains Mixup and adds AugMix multi-chain perturbations with Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD) consistency regularization to strengthen invariance under diverse corruptions. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, along with their corruption benchmarks CIFAR-10-C and CIFAR-100-C, compare the proposed method with Random Erasing, Mixup, CutMix, AutoAugment, and AugMix. Results show that the proposed strategy improves clean accuracy and reduces mean corruption error (mCE), confirming the complementary benefits of cross-sample interpolation and multi-perturbation consistency regularization and offering a simple and effective training recipe for robust image classification.

Document Title: Cross-Subject Three-Class EEG Emotion Recognition Using a Lightweight EEGNet Pipeline on the REFED-2025 Dataset
Author Affiliations: Department of Computer Science, University of Maryland, College Park, College Park, MD, USA
Publication Title: 2026 7th International Seminar on Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Information Technology (AINIT)
Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition remains challenging because of low signal-to-noise ratio, inter-subject variability, and limited training data. This paper presents a lightweight three-class EEG emotion-recognition pipeline for the REFED-2025 dataset using trial-level valence labeling, band-pass filtering, downsampling, one-second segmentation, channel-wise normalization, and EEGNet classification. The evaluation follows a rigorous 5-fold subject-level cross-validation setting to ensure subject-independent robustness, with 3000 sampled training windows per fold. EEGNet is compared with SimpleCNN, MLP, and a traditional Differential Entropy based SVM (DE-SVM) baseline, while Gaussian noise injection is further examined. EEGNet achieves an average accuracy of 41.25±2.14%, marginally outperforming DE-SVM and other baselines, while obtaining a macro-F1 score of 0.31±0.02. The ablation results show that simple Gaussian noise injection leads to a severe performance degradation (dropping accuracy to 32.31%), indicating that basic noise augmentation is insufficient under extreme data scarcity and complex cross-subject variability. These findings indicate that while compact EEG-specific architectures provide a parameter-efficient baseline on REFED-2025, they struggle with imbalanced class distribution, and traditional feature engineering remains highly competitive under data scarcity.

Document Title: Noise-Robust Deep Learning for RF-Based Drone Identification: A Leakage-Audited SNR Benchmark on the DroneRF Dataset
Author Affiliations: Division of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (Drone System Major), Kyungwoon University, Gumi, Republic of Korea
Abstract: Deep learning classifiers report near-perfect accuracy on the widely used DroneRF drone-identification benchmark, but typically under clean signals and sample-level train/test splits that scatter slices of one acquisition across both sides. This paper rebuilds the benchmark with the leakage controlled and measured: splits that group every slice of a recorded segment, a stricter time-block protocol with guard gaps (the 227 segments come from ten captures), an audit of what the sample-level shortcut leaks, raw-signal noise injection whose effect on the model’s input is measured, not assumed, and every headline result averaged over five splits and three seeds with 95% confidence intervals. Under this protocol we benchmark six model variants (a compact convolutional network, ResNet-18, EfficientNet-B0, and ViT-Small, the last two also ImageNet-pretrained) and five training policies, including an AugMix baseline. Clean-trained models approach single-class prediction at −20 dB raw signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) — which class survives varies by run and architecture—while random-SNR injection, which matches the best policy at usable SNRs with no anchor or schedule, restores 67–86% accuracy at −10 dB; on the compact network this costs two points of clean accuracy and a 25% chunk false-alarm rate (4% after segment voting). A DroneDetect replication, with test subsets recorded under real Bluetooth and Wi-Fi interference, bounds the approach: interference degrades noise- and clean-trained models by margins we cannot separate, so no transfer of Gaussian-noise robustness is detectable. All code and per-run results are released; the pipeline is deterministic.

Document Title: Pre-trained Under Noise: A Framework for Robust Bone Fracture Detection in Medical Imaging
Authors: R. Hoover; N. Elsayed; Z. ElSayed; C. Li
Author Affiliations: School of Information Technology, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio; School of Information Technology, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio; School of Information Technology, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio; School of Information Technology, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on Computing and Machine Intelligence (ICMI)
Abstract: Medical Imagings are considered one of the crucial diagnostic tools for different bones-related diseases, especially bones fractures. This paper investigates the robustness of pre-trained deep learning models for classifying bone fractures in X-ray images and seeks to address global healthcare disparity through the lens of technology. Three deep learning models have been tested under varying simulated equipment quality conditions. ResNet50, VGG16 and EfficientNetv2 are the three pre-trained architectures which are compared. These models were used to perform bone fracture classification as images were progressively degraded using noise. This paper specifically empirically studies how the noise can affect the bone fractures detection and how the pre-trained models performance can be changes due to the noise that affect the quality of the X-ray images. This paper aims to help replicate real world challenges experienced by medical imaging technicians across the world. Thus, this paper establishes a methodological framework for assessing AI model degradation using transfer learning and controlled noise augmentation. The findings provide practical insight into how robust and generalizable different pre-trained deep learning powered computer vision models can be when used in different contexts.
